correctness.rationale: Every one of the 16 vertices, 8008 six-subsets, and 11440 seven-subsets is explicitly regenerated. Two independently constructed closed balls and two signature implementations agree on all 19448 tested subsets; no six-subset qualifies and exactly 960 seven-subsets do. The complete 384-element Hamming-isometry group is generated and checked to preserve every closed ball. Three full orbits have sizes 192,384,384 and stabilizer orders 2,1,1; invariant pair-distance spectra prove inequivalence. The three orbits exhaust the 960 minima. Independent Burnside fixed-point enumeration yields 1152=3*384. The Gray map is tested on every ordered pair in the Lee torus Z4^2, confirming equivalence of the published census. No infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: Critical overlap was found and incorporated: the earlier Kim--Kim theorem already establishes the minimum 7 and exact 960 labeled codes for the isomorphic Lee graph. The new claim is only the full three-orbit Hamming-isometry classification and three intrinsic distance distributions. The earlier source prints two examples belonging to the 192 and one 384 orbit but not the third 384 orbit. Comparison with earlier binary Hamming work and exact-claim/alias searches revealed no source giving or implying the three types; an obscure or unindexed equivalent orbit census remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: No targeted search can exclude an obscure or unindexed historical classification of the same 960 minima into three orbits.
The 2015 degree-four Abelian Cayley-graph article was available at abstract and metadata level only; no full-document noncoverage conclusion is asserted for it.

value.rationale: The equality case of the smallest nontrivial binary four-dimensional one-identification problem is a canonical finite sensor placement classification, not an arbitrary slice. Although optimum size and all-code count were already known, the full equivalence structure was unresolved in the inspected exact-parameter source: all 960 optima reduce to exactly three geometries with independently distinguishing Hamming-distance spectra. The earlier full census printed only two example geometries, making the missing third type and exact stabilizers a concrete and reusable addition to code classification and symmetry-reduced search.
